**City Core prime office rent is £95–£100 psf on the headline brokers' latest readings (JLL moved to £100.00 psf in Q3 2026 [F57]); Savills' achieved-rent measure is £116.73 psf [F25].**

| Broker | Figure | Period | Measure | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JLL | £100.00 psf | 2026Q3 | prime rent ("City") | [F57] |
| JLL | £95.00 psf | 2026Q2 | prime rent, incentives 24 months on 10-yr term ("City") | [F68] |
| Cushman & Wakefield | £95 psf | 2026Q2 | prime headline rent, rental map (City Core, exact) | [F94] |
| BNP Paribas | £95.00 psf | 2026Q2 | prime rent, premium rent reported separately ("City") | [F12] |
| Avison Young | £97.50 psf | 2026Q2 | prime rent, quoted for Northern City/Broadgate (approximate) | [F105] |
| Savills | £116.73 psf | 2026Q2 | average *achieved* prime rent, H1 2026 ("City") | [F25] |

Points to note:
- JLL is the only broker with a 2026Q3 City prime rent in the store; the others' latest is Q2 2026.
- These are not the same measure. BNP Paribas quotes a *premium* rent of £150.00 psf for amenity-rich assets (top floor with terrace) separately from its £95.00 prime [F12]; Savills derives its figure from achieved rents rather than ERVs [F25]; Avison Young's £97.50 is its Northern City/Broadgate quoting area, not the whole City Core [F105].
- Only Cushman & Wakefield's £95 psf is an exact City Core fit [F94]; the rest are approximate mappings to the "City".

I have not blended these into a single market figure — they measure different things.
